summary: grep searches text and prints the lines that match a pattern. Use it to find errors in a log, a name in a list, or a word in every file of a project.
notes: grep miles prints nothing because the file has Miles with a capital M. grep -i miles finds both lines.
"^A" is a regular expression: ^ matches the start of a line, so Maya does not match even though it contains a.
In cat cs/grades.csv | grep ",10," | wc -l, the commas make 10 match only the grade column, not part of a score like 100. wc -l then counts the 10th graders.
pitfall: When grep finds nothing it prints nothing, which looks the same as a command that did not run. Check spelling and capitals, or add -i, before you decide the text is not there.
